text_blocks.snippet: Alexander Graham Bell is officially credited with patenting and inventing the first practical telephone.

list.snippet: Patent Date: Alexander Graham Bell received US Patent No. 174,465 on March 7, 1876.
First Words: On March 10, 1876, he spoke the famous first words to his assistant Thomas Watson: "Mr. Watson, come here, I want to see you."
Inspiration: His work with speech and acoustics was heavily influenced by his mother's hearing loss and his career teaching deaf students.

Antonio Meucci: The Italian-born inventor developed an early voice-communication device called the "teletrofono" in 1854. In 2002, the U.S. House of Representatives passed a resolution recognizing Meucci's pioneering work in the invention of the telephone.
Elisha Gray: Gray filed a patent caveat for a similar telephone design on the exact same day as Bell (February 14, 1876), leading to a famous legal race for the patent.
